notes.content:
Some adventures should never end…

[h3]This winter, rediscover Benoît Sokal’s clockpunk universe with [i]Syberia - Remastered[/i]![/h3]

[previewyoutube=SqHihFXG9Kc;full][/previewyoutube]
More than 20 years after its original release, [i]Syberia[/i] is reborn in a [b]fully modernized version[/b]. Rediscover its iconic locations and unforgettable characters through a stunning visual overhaul, redesigned gameplay, and the same captivating storytelling that made it a classic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/6640461/dcbedecbb4164d22390be18daced5ced183dd716.jpg[/img]
[b]Kate Walker[/b], a brilliant lawyer from New York, is sent to a remote village in the French Alps to finalize the sale of an old automaton factory. But what begins as a routine assignment soon turns into an extraordinary journey across Eastern Europe and its snow-covered landscapes.

Accompanied by [b]Oscar[/b], a loyal and one-of-a-kind automaton, Kate sets out to explore mysterious and forgotten places, filled with eccentric characters, as she follows the trail of Hans Voralberg, a genius inventor pursuing a seemingly impossible dream: finding the last living mammoths on the mythical island of Syberia.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/6640461/50fb9ad754c3fce325a283e86562d1c7f2de17e2.jpg[/img]
An unexpected, thrilling, and deeply emotional voyage that will challenge everything she thought she knew. First released in 2002, [i]Syberia[/i] became [b]a reference in the adventure genre[/b], praised for its unique atmosphere, sharp writing, and the richness of Benoît Sokal’s artistic vision. This remaster is a new opportunity to (re)discover the masterpiece, following in the footsteps of other titles from Benoît Sokal such as “[i][b]Syberia: The World Before[/b][/i]” and the newly released “[i][b]Amerzone: The Explorer’s Legacy[/b][/i]”.

notes.title: Amerzone – The Explorer’s Legacy (PC) Review
notes.content:
I know I say this a lot, but I was genuinely surprised by Amerzone: The Explorer’s Legacy. Not just because of the content of the game itself, but the—for lack of a better word—legacy that this game carries with it. As I’ve mentioned before, I never had a competent gaming PC growing up, and as such, I missed out on many of the biggest games to dominate the space.

But Amerzone’s 1999 PC release had quite the pedigree behind it. Not only was it an extension of designer Benoît Sokal’s comic strip L’Amerzone, but it would also become the first entry in the long-running Syberia series. It’s genuinely nice to see so many of the point-and-click puzzle games that defined the genre getting glow-ups, and much like Myst before it, Amerzone: The Explorer’s Legacy is enhanced by years of gaming innovation.

notes.title: 🔎 A closer look at Microids Studio Paris, creator of the Amerzone remake
notes.content:
Benoît Sokal’s iconic adventure game, [i]Amerzone - The Explorer's Legacy[/i], is about to return with an ambitious remake that’s more immersive than ever. Here, you can learn more about the designers behind the game...

[h2]“We work well together as a team”[/h2]

This remake of [i]Amerzone[/i] – a faithful update that promises some new features – is in the hands of Microids Studio Paris. Formed in October 2021, the team has been built around former developers from the studio Koalabs, maker of [i]Syberia 3[/i] and [i]Syberia: The World Before[/i]. Today, it includes more than 60 members, working at the headquarters of Microids in the 19th arrondissement of Paris. “[i]Being on the same premises as our publisher is a plus point,[/i]” Antoine Babary, Audio Director, told us. “[i]It helps us communicate more smoothly and make decisions faster.[/i]”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915176/3e76daf9683225a56c7d75b30de501c1c836d31b.jpg[/img]

According to the team members, the human size of Microids Studio Paris creates a close and supportive environment. “[i]When we have an idea to improve the game, we can talk about it and reach a decision pretty fast, without having to deal with layers of hierarchy,[/i]” Édouard Bourgeat, Principal Sound Designer, stated. “[i]We work well together as a team; most of the members have already delivered at least one game together,[/i]” added Grégory Chicoine, Level Designer. “[i]Delivery is a high-pressure stage in development, which proves the ability to work together.[/i]”

[h2]Experts in Sokal-esque adventure games[/h2]

Through its work on the [i]Syberia[/i] series over the years, Microids Studio Paris has developed expertise in the adventure game genre. “[i]Working on [/i]Syberia [i]allowed me to level up my skills, particularly with camera angles: what do we want to show, and how to show it?[/i]”, Grégory explained. “[i]This experience with [/i]Syberia[i] helped me a lot with [/i]Amerzone[i]; we started out on a solid basis.[/i]”

The studio's background with [i]Syberia[/i] means that it masters the world of Benoît Sokal better than anyone. “[i]From the music to the visuals and the mechanics, there are many similarities between [/i]Syberia [i]and [/i]Amerzone[i]. By understanding one, we can enhance the other,[/i]” Antoine pointed out. “[i]What’s more, our creative leads have a long history of collaboration with Benoît; they know his work inside out,[/i]” added Édouard. “[i]This means we can produce a remake of [/i]Amerzone[i] that’s as close as possible to what Benoît would have wanted.[/i]”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915176/ed8f473fa7c46e682d755dec72e67ec219b75d67.jpg[/img]

Furthermore, Microids Studio Paris has been honing its skills with its tool of choice, the Unity engine, achieving ever greater performance. “Syberia [i]and[/i] Amerzone [i]share a lot of technologies,[/i]” Grégory explained. “[i]The foundations were already there, allowing us to focus on improvements and new features, like the point-of-view and sequence shots.[/i]”

[h2]Creating a remake that lives up to the cult game[/h2]

Thanks to its expertise in adventure games, its solid development processes and its deep knowledge of Benoît Sokal’s work, the studio firmly believes that it can deliver the remake of [i]Amerzone[/i] that players deserve. “[i]With our background, we’re confident that we’re well positioned to meet the expectations,[/i]” stated Édouard. “[i]The team has risen to all the challenges, and has strived to push the experience as far as possible,[/i]” added Antoine. “[i]I really believe we can be proud of what we’ve accomplished,[/i]” Grégory concluded.

notes.title: 🎵 Dive into the music of the remake, with acclaimed composer Inon Zur
notes.content:
You will soon be able to discover or rediscover [i]Amerzone[/i], the first video-game masterpiece by [i]Benoît Sokal (Syberia)[/i], through an ambitious remake featuring cutting-edge graphics and newly composed tracks. We reveal all in this article!

[h2]🎻 The works of composer Inon Zur and his son Ori [/h2]

To create a fresh soundtrack for the remake of [b]Amerzone[/b], Microids Studio Paris once again turned to [b]Inon Zur[/b], the internationally-renowned composer and author of the music for Syberia over the past two decades. “[i]I worked with Benoît Sokal for many years, and I liked him a lot, both as a person and an artist,[/i]” Inon Zur told us. “[i]For me, it’s always a blast to be involved in another one of his incredible works.[/i]”

This time, however, Inon is not composing alone; he has brought his son on board! “[i]Ori graduated from the music department of Northwestern University two years ago, and he’s been composing ever since,[/i]” said Inon. “[i]When Microids contacted me, I said to myself that it would be the perfect chance to work with Ori, and for him to show his talent.[/i]” Inon created Amerzone’s main theme and the journey theme, while Ori composed the rest of the music.

To find inspiration, the pair immersed themselves in Amerzone’s visual and narrative dimensions, giving free expression to their feelings. “[i]Composers need to connect with their emotions when they watch a work and discover its story, then translate those emotions into music,[/i]” Inon explained to us. In the case of Amerzone, those emotions may be bitterness about a wonderful world that has fallen into ruins... as well as the hope of restoring its former glory.

During the creative process, Inon decided to give only technical advice to his son, avoiding any further interference in his work. “[i]Music is a highly personal thing,[/i]” stated the composer. “[i]So I chose to stand back and let Ori express his own style. I can tell you that he contributes something unique, and that I was very impressed.[/i]”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915176/aaf7eef7325be3b791d4986d377233124b983570.jpg[/img]

[h2]🎼 Intimate music that tells a story[/h2]

The end product delivered by Inon and Ori Zur is primarily orchestral music, complemented by ethnic touches that immerse us in the jungle of Amerzone. Ranging from guitar to flute and percussion, the composers used instruments with various styles and origins, to avoid linking the music with a specific place and allow the listener to drift into an imaginary world. “[i]This is also achieved by the way in which the instruments are played,[/i]” added Inon Zur. “[i]We take a classical guitar, for example, and use it in an unusual way to create an exotic feel for players.[/i]”

Following the spectacular atmosphere of [i]Syberia[/i], [b]Amerzone[/b] takes us into something much more intimate. This is why [i]Inon and Ori[/i] decided to play some of the instruments themselves this time, including the guitar and flute. With each track, their aim is to support the narrative: “[i]The music tells a story first and foremost,[/i]” stated Inon. “[i]It allows us to create the tension that makes players want to find out what will happen next.[/i]”

For the composer, this latest soundtrack made with his son really hit the mark. “[i]It’s a great source of pride and joy to see Ori carry the baton, and I think that he did an excellent job,[/i]” enthused Inon. “[i]The thing that I like most about Amerzone is that each piece of music is different; however, once they are assembled, they fit together perfectly, like the pieces of a puzzle.[/i]”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915176/992bb759fc0ec519ab1caa924005b713df8ed19b.png[/img]

notes.title: 🕊️ A visual overhaul to amaze us once again 🎨
notes.content:
25 years ago, [i]Amerzone - The Explorer's Legacy[/i] blew away audiences and laid the foundations of the adventure genre, with its singular atmosphere and groundbreaking visuals. This year, the remake designed by Microids Studio Paris is on track to pull off a similar feat! We took a closer look at the huge effort the team is putting into the graphics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915176/1ef5e163593b6eebb9545ddf9500324b987bc158.png[/img]

[h2]Fresh visuals that enhance the game experience[/h2]

From the outset of development, the ambition was clear: virtually all of [i]Amerzone[/i]’s visual elements needed to be redesigned for the remake arriving this autumn. From the textured 3D models to the lighting effects, almost everything was recreated from scratch using modern techniques. “[i]Much of our focus was on the vegetation and water, which feature heavily in the scenery,[/i]” explained Xavier Tual and Frédéric Gesquière, the pair in charge of artistic direction at Microids Studio Paris. “[i]We worked on making the foliage varied and luxuriant, and bringing realism to the various rivers, lakes and swamps that the players will discover over the course of their adventure.[/i]”

In addition to the environments, the characters were given special attention in this ambitious remake. Each one was remodeled and based on the original drawings of the creator Benoît Sokal, in order to bring out all their splendor and surpass the technical limits of 1999. Then, for the first time, they were animated using motion capture. “[i]This allows us to reproduce the subtleties of an actor's performance, and achieve a result that’s as human as possible,[/i]” told us Xavier. “[i]The characters in [/i]Amerzone[i] have been marked by life; their faces are windows into their personalities.[/i]”

Another new visual and technological feature: all the environments and characters are now displayed in real time, in contrast with the fixed images that were used in the original game. “[i]Real-time 3D brings things to life; we can feel the wind in the trees, see the birds take off and the water move,[/i]” commented Frédéric. “[i]It also creates depth; it makes it possible to observe the surroundings and objects from different angles.[/i]” To create this lush world, Microids Studio Paris has pushed the engine Unity to the limits, building on the expertise it demonstrated in 2022 with [i]Syberia: The World Before[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915176/78ee14319ffab39f06952e20b1eb75916bb0f833.jpg[/img]

[h2]Redesigned graphics that stay true to the original[/h2]

While transforming [i]Amerzone[/i]’s graphics to bring them up to today’s standards, the team set itself the goal of remaining faithful to the original release. “[i]One thing that hasn’t changed a bit is the atmosphere and overall feel,[/i]” Xavier assured us. “[i]Our aim is to enhance all of the content of the original game, […] to fully realize Benoît Sokal’s vision, without the technical limits that constrained his creativity at the time,[/i]” added Frédéric. A few things have been left as they were though, like the sketches in Valembois’ notebook, which have simply been put in high definition to enjoy them as never before.

To strike the fine balance between innovation and respect for the source, the teams at Microids Studio Paris spent a lot of time replaying the original title and returned to Benoît Sokal working files. “[i]We asked ourselves what the essential elements were that needed to be kept, and what we could add to the game without straying too far from the original,[/i]” told us Xavier. “[i]Take the iconic temple for example, with its Mayan-style architecture, surrounded by rock and lava. We kept all of that, while polishing it to make it even more brilliant![/i]” To achieve its goal, the team has been able to rely on the vast experience gained working alongside Benoît Sokal over nearly a decade; as well as on his family, who have been looking after his legacy since he left us.

The result? A visual overhaul that should both live up to the expectations of the original fans, and wow new audiences.

notes.title: 🕊️ What new gameplay features can we expect to see in the remake? 🎮
notes.content:
This year, players will get a chance to discover or revisit Benoît Sokal’s first masterpiece – [i]Amerzone[/i]. Previously, we looked at how the remake will remain faithful to the 1999 original; we will now take a peek at some totally new features in the pipeline, beginning with game mechanics. Let’s get started!

[h2]Which mechanics to update and which to leave as they are?[/h2]

This was our first question: how does Microids Studio Paris identify which mechanics from the original version should be kept and which should be modernized. Romain Pierson, Game Designer, gave the following explanation: “[i]We started by spending a lot of time playing the original title, to check each mechanic for playability and clarity.[/i]” The team also looks at how today’s audiences like to play, and checks whether [i]Amerzone[/i]’s gameplay is still compatible. “[i]In the 1999 version, players only had to click once on a lever to pull it down; today, players wouldn’t find that satisfying enough.[/i]” Romain offered as an example. Lastly, the highly positive reviews of [i]Syberia: The World Before[/i], Microids Studio Paris’ previous adventure game, highlighted mechanics that were well received by players and could be added to [i]Amerzone[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915176/5c5a4c5b563a65fa56783ac82371340289788471.jpg[/img]

[h2]Gameplay innovations integrated in the remake[/h2]

With this in mind, which gameplay elements are being transformed in the remake? “[i]First, there are the puzzles and the way players interact with objects,[/i]” told us Amanda Goengrich, Concept Artist. “[i]In the original game, everything was very static. Now, as in [/i]Syberia: The World Before[i], players can enjoy turning objects around in their hands, observing them, and figuring out how they work. As Benoît Sokal liked to say, in reference to Little Red Riding Hood,[/i] ‘pull the peg and the latch will drop’”. In addition to all the puzzles from the original, which have been made more dynamic and organic, you will also find some fresh challenges that offer surprises and keep the game going longer. 

Another new gameplay feature in store in [i]Amerzone[/i] is the addition of a diary, packed with functional and narrative elements. There, players will find objectives and optional clues to help them, as well as notes about the adventure taken by the player character, an inventory, documents, and an investigation tab. “[i]The investigation system is another innovation in this remake,[/i]” commented Amanda. “[i]As a journalist, our character can choose to dig deeper into something that piques their interest, with a view to writing an article about it. These investigations are kind of like side missions.[/i]”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915176/70e2fadbd62341ae60c65837cfaaf7149d44e673.png[/img]

Next, in this remake, [i]Amerzone[/i] has been tweaked in various ways to enhance and modernize the game experience. In particular, much effort has gone into the transitions between scenes: while they used to be instantaneous, there are now real movements where the player is totally immersed in the character. There is also a fast movement function to rapidly backtrack, and players will find automatic saves at numerous checkpoints. “[i]We now also offer two difficulty levels – Journey and Adventure – that give a choice between getting a bit more guidance or playing with total independence,[/i]” Romain added. “[i]And we’ve also been working hard to make sure that [/i]Amerzone[i] is equally playable using a mouse and keyboard, and a PlayStation or Xbox controller.[/i]”

[h2]A game experience for both fans and newcomers![/h2]

“[i]We are creating this remake for fans of the original title, who will find everything they loved about [/i]Amerzone[i], along with our added little improvements,[/i]” concluded Amanda. “[i]But it’s also for new players who enjoy story-based games, deep thinking and being transported into imaginary worlds.[/i]”

This is a great chance to discover or rediscover [i]Amerzone[/i], with reviewed and improved gameplay!

notes.title: 🕊️ Here’s how the remake of Amerzone keeps the soul of the original game 🐣
notes.content:
With its remake of [i]Amerzone - The Explorer's Legacy[/i], Microids Studio Paris is bringing a classic adventure game up to date, and not just with new graphics. At the same time, the team is painstakingly preserving the identity of the original episode, released in 1999. We took a look at how they are managing this balancing act!

[h2]Handling a classic game with respect[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915176/12f496b9f478c0e77435cfead3f167333ef77214.jpg[/img]

For Microids Studio Paris, whose team worked with Benoît Sokal for nearly a decade, it was crucial to honor the work of this unique author. As Lucas Lagravette, Game Director, told us: “[i]We see it as a piece of history. It’s a title that has earned cult status with its atmosphere and narrative world; so, we could never allow ourselves to treat it lightly.[/i]”

To succeed in creating a remake that is both faithful and innovative, the designers drew inspiration from Capcom’s approach to [i]Resident Evil[/i] on the GameCube. “[i]It was a remake that enhanced the experience, while respecting the original and its audience,[/i]” commented Lucas. He gave the following example: “[i]There’s a really well-known corridor in [/i]Resident Evil[i], where dogs jump in through the windows. This doesn’t happen in the remake, so players let down their guard. It’s only when returning later that the dogs finally appear, offering a surprise for even the earliest fans! It’s a great example of how to use a subtle change to augment the source game.[/i]”

With the [i]Amerzone[/i] remake, Microids Studio Paris has had to decide what should remain the same, and what should be adjusted or redesigned. To guide this process, as Lucas Lagravette explained to us, some general principles were laid down as early as the pre-production phase, following analysis of the 1999 version and other references. “[i]Then, during production, there are lots of decisions to make on a case-by-case basis,[/i]” added the Game Director. “[i]Part of my job is to make these decisions – in consultation with Benoît Sokal’s family, and with the help of the talented team that we worked with to make [/i]Syberia: The World Before.”

[h2]Features of Amerzone that will be kept in the remake[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915176/136781db382998d0d7e04832303b234d7f7d83ec.jpg[/img]

So, what won’t be changing in the [i]Amerzone[/i] remake? Firstly, as you may have noticed in the trailers, the player's character still moves from one scene to the next in a linear fashion. “[i]We experimented with allowing free movement, but it just didn’t feel like [/i]Amerzone,” Lucas told us. “[i]The levels aren’t designed that way; a typical example being the lighthouse, which is tall and narrow. We also believe that this kind of unusual way of moving around will be a differentiating feature of our game.[/i]”

Similarly, the character controlled by players will remain out of frame and silent, as in the 1999 game. Lucas Lagravette commented on this choice: “[i]If we had given a voice to the protagonist, we would also have had to come up with a character, a past and motivations... But [/i]Amerzone[i] was never about the hero. The player's character is intentionally silent, because it’s all about exploring an incredible world, with its enchanting and tragic story, through their eyes.”

Another feature that will remain similar to the original [i]Amerzone[/i] is its ambiguous story. Unlike [i]Syberia: The World Before[/i], which has a strong narrative thread, [i]Amerzone[/i] was always minimalistic. Lucas confirmed to us that this aspect will not be changing in the remake: “[i]Even when we introduce totally new scenes, things will never be clearly explained. It’s important for us to keep these gray areas, which can be read in different ways by players, lying beneath the surface of the gripping plot.[/i]”

Going by these few examples and many others awaiting you in the final game, to be released in [b]autumn 2024[/b] on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series, the remake of [i]Amerzone[/i] will clearly be an authentic tribute to the original episode. 25 years after its first release, this experience is as relevant as ever, with timeless themes like adventure, totalitarianism and disillusion.

notes.title: 🕊️ A look back at what made the 1999 original so magical! ✨
notes.content:
A great classic of the adventure genre that sold more than a million copies, [i]Amerzone[/i] is returning with an ambitious remake to mark its twenty-fifth anniversary. So, what was it that made the original game so brilliant? Let’s refresh our memories together in this article!

[h2]A stunning visual atmosphere that stood out from the rest[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915176/8d59d08a2e9abde8e54f52b722fa66ae8bec7e83.png[/img]
The first thing to grab players’ attention when they loaded up [i]Amerzone[/i] was its visual appearance. They could explore pre-rendered 3D environments that went beyond anything possible in real-time in those days. “[i]It went even further than [/i]Resident Evil[i], for example, which had fixed pre-rendered scenes[/i],” Lucas Lagravette added, Game Director at Microids Studio Paris. “[i]In [/i]Amerzone[i], it was possible to turn the camera 360 degrees and become totally immersed in the world.[/i]”

This world was an amazing jungle, offering plenty of realism and yet inhabited by imaginary plants and animals. Players would often wonder if what they were seeing on their screens was real or made-up. “[i]This was the signature of the creator Benoît Sokal[/i],” Lucas Lagravette explained. “[i]There was a kind of ‘austereness’ in Benoît’s fantasy world, which made the illusion all the more effective. It’s impossible to separate [/i]Amerzone[i] from Benoît Sokal; it truly is an art game and it always had a special place in his heart.[/i]”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915176/027decf2975bb405d20203a6439f63c4d4e06b87.jpg[/img]
[h2]An engrossing narrative with a deep subtext[/h2]

Benoît Sokal, who sadly left us in 2021, put a great deal of work into the atmosphere in [i]Amerzone[/i], for instance by drawing all the sketches in Valembois' notebook. He was also a great storyteller; the narrative in [i]Amerzone[/i] is another thing that marked players at the time.

“[i]Players learned more about the world through a letter here, a phone call there, or an amazing cutscene. This way of conveying the story wasn’t common in 1999[/i],” Lucas Lagravette recalled. [i]Amerzone[/i] also carried messages to be discovered between the lines, on topics such as colonialism, dictatorship and endangered species.

For players to interact with the story, the original team opted for point-and-click gameplay: another contributing factor to the title’s massive appeal. “[i]The game mechanics are accessible, involving no great skill or time pressure|/i],” Lucas told us. “[i]All you need is patience![/i]”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915176/ed49c3326e2bf0f9dbd68ae2221c9d3fcc160cee.png[/img]
[h2]Amerzone: a timeless title, worthy of a remake[/h2]

A visual environment that’s both familiar and mysterious; a rich and immersive story; and game mechanics that allow players to explore at their own pace: these are the things that made [i]Amerzone[/i] so special.

And the game remains relevant today, whether it’s for the message that’s still topical, Benoît Sokal’s unique artistic signature, or our enduring need to escape into fantastical worlds.

The release of a remake that will enhance the original experience is a golden chance to dive back into [i]Amerzone[/i] or discover it for the first time.
